FAIL.summary: A certificate has expired, has invalid dates or exceeds the configured maximum lifetime of {{maxCertificateLifetimeDays}} days.
actions: Find the failed certificate in the credential tables and note its source object, name and expiry date.

For an app registration certificate, open App registrations > this application > Certificates & secrets. For an enterprise application's SAML signing certificate, open Enterprise applications > this application > Single sign-on > SAML Signing Certificate.
Coordinate with the application team to replace the certificate with one whose dates meet the configured lifetime limit. Update the application's trust or deployed credential as needed.
Confirm that the application uses the replacement before removing an old credential. Run the report again to confirm that no certificate date failures remain.

WARN.summary: A credential expires soon, is not yet valid, or a client secret has a date-policy problem. The expiry warning window is {{credentialWarningDays}} days.
actions: Check the credential tables for the affected object and dates. Secrets have a maximum lifetime of {{maxSecretLifetimeDays}} days; certificates have a maximum lifetime of {{maxCertificateLifetimeDays}} days.
Arrange rotation with the application team before expiry, or correct an unsuitable start date. Prefer federation where supported.
Verify the replacement is in use before removing old credentials, then collect a new report.

UNKNOWN.summary: Credential dates could not be evaluated from the collected metadata.
actions: Ask the report administrator to check credential collection errors and Application.Read.All consent.
Collect a new report with readable credential start and end dates. Do not treat an unknown date as a valid credential.
